PE landscape overview

The Private-equity landscape maps 35 sponsors that compete with BSP for lower-middle-market business and consumer services deals. BSP is among the smallest funds on the map, so its edge rests on co-invest capacity and operating credibility rather than fund size (Private-equity landscape, Sep 24, 2026).

Where BSP sits

  • The main fund reports $335M sold as of April 2025 (BSP firm profile).
  • Rival flagships run $0.9–2.1B: Trivest VII at $950M, Bertram V at $1.5B and Gridiron V at $2.1B (Private-equity landscape).
  • The $50–250M equity-check band is unverified (BSP firm profile).
  • The closest thesis peers are MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram. MidOcean VI closed at $1.5B in 2023, with $50–300M+ checks (Private-equity landscape).

Competition by portfolio company

Portfolio companyMain sponsor-backed rivalsPosition
Punctual ProsSila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc)Most crowded; avoid auctions
CETKohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult), Huron (Criticore, Albireo)Open space in New England
FrontlineAlpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVNo direct sponsor-backed copy
Thomas ScientificCalibre ScientificMain bidder for U.S. add-ons

What the filings add

  • Home services is splitting in two. Scaled rivals borrow at S+425–475, marked at par. TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber pay part of their interest in kind (PIK) and are marked at 89–94 (Competitor filings).
  • Horizon has at least $211M of first-lien debt at one lender, marked at 92.5. Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026. Both are more likely to sell assets than to bid for add-ons (Competitor filings).
  • Sila's revenue is est. $450–650M, low confidence (Competitor filings).
  • IES can pay strategic prices for New England contractors. It earns 11.4% operating margins and carries no net debt (Competitor filings).
  • Stretched add-on pacing has hurt sponsors before. Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them (Home-services company case studies).

Gaps and caveats

  • Web search quota ran out partway through the research. Later firms were checked mainly against their own websites.
  • Fund sizes for Gryphon VI, Trilantic VII, Palladium VI, Tailwind IV and Shore Business Services II are unknown.
  • Rivals for BPI and Fair Harbor are not covered in the shown landscape implications. A peer list of comms and apparel sponsors would close that gap.
  • Leverage and EBITDA figures for rivals are estimates, because each source shows only one lender's slice.

Next actions

  1. Build a proprietary outreach list of sub-$3M EBITDA HVAC and plumbing shops in Punctual Pros' counties. Lean on Authority Brands territory rights.
  2. Track Horizon and Heartland lender actions ahead of Dec 15, 2026 for possible asset sales.
  3. Prioritise CET add-ons in New England before Albireo's Upstate NY expansion reaches the region.
  4. Fill the missing fund sizes and the BPI and Fair Harbor peer sets once search capacity resets.
